scope: Scene01 actual bank terrain, stone/water boundaries, scan material energy and bridge-pier ground contact. Camera, sun, environment intensity, exposure and water shader remain at R07.

diagnosis.method: Official1254 low courtyard ray picks on unchanged R07 source
causes: Earth color times dark procedural map produces near-black soil
Broad1.8m smooth route shoulders and three giant rounded soil masses obscure natural water boundaries
Scan recoloring and added moss cover much of each stone with a similar olive finish

geometry: Continuous closed terraced shore and local bridge inlet; route-distance blending carries the actual route foundations without abrupt cliffs
Route bank falloff contracts from1.8m to1.25m and three oversized buried soil mounds are omitted
63 additional placements of the retained full3D CC0 stone scans form drowned toes, short middle/upper strata and court-face receiver courses
Existing shore stones are lowered where the new ground would otherwise leave them floating; actual cascade lips are held
Two stepped closed granite pier shoes extend into the new inlet bed by at least.12m and overlap original pier bases by.16m
Small shore pebbles use centerY=terrainY+.30s and verticalRadius=.70s, embedding their lower.40s into actual ground
New creased sedge blades and dry root runs occupy sparse actual crevices; three rooted flower shelves retain a lower azalea hierarchy
materials: Original scan geometry/UV/color/normal assets retained with sparse slope-dependent moss and height-dependent wet roughness
Sparse physically closed surface-conformed moss skins replace the broad olive coating; detached moss balls are muted while retaining original RNG consumption
Mineral soil reflectance and world-stable grain/gravel/root shading replace the black double-tinted earth
preserved: R07 foreground craft, temple/pagoda/bridge architecture and camera
Actual scene-reflecting water shader and source asset identities
limitations: Inherited bridge-end shrub volume remains visibly simplified; later alternative shrubs/large rock spurs were rejected and retained outside this candidate
Some route-facing soil/masonry surfaces and geological repetition remain visible
The bank is an authored interpretation, not surveyed geology
Full scene remains short of HD01 photographic fidelity
